subject: mathematics
question_text: Find the equation of the plane passing through A(3, −2, −1) and parallel to the vectors b = i − 2j + 4k and c = 3i + 2j − 5k.

mark_split.label: Write the point and the two vectors
State that b × c is the normal
Write the Cartesian equation and check

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.79, chapter 7 PRODUCT OF VECTORS, Long Answer question 9. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1+2+1+1+2 split pays two marks for the cross product that produces the normal and two for the closing Cartesian form, where the point and both directions are checked. Paper position: Maths-1A Section C prints 3 long answers at 8 marks each and the student answers any 2; Product of Vectors is one of the units that can fill a Section-C slot. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find the equation of a plane through a point and parallel to two given vectors.

steps.label: Write what is given
steps.margin_note: First mark. The point comes as a coordinate triple and the two directions come already in vector form, so only the point has to be converted.
steps.memory_tip: Only the point needs converting. The two directions are already vectors.

recall.must_convey: That the point is written as a = 3i − 2j − k and the two given direction vectors are noted.
accept: write the point as three i minus two j minus k
note a b and c before starting
the two directions are already in i j k form
point ni vector ga rasta, directions already vectors
a is three i minus two j minus k

steps.why: The plane equation needs a point vector and a normal vector. The point is the only piece here that is not already a vector.
common_mistakes: Missing the minus signs on the second and third coordinates of A.
Treating b and c as points of the plane instead of directions.

steps.label: State the normal direction
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The two given vectors are parallel to the plane, not inside it, but a vector at right angles to both is still at right angles to the plane. That sentence earns the mark.
steps.memory_tip: Parallel to the plane is enough. A vector at right angles to both is the normal.
lines: The plane is parallel to both b and c.
b × c is at right angles to b and to c,
so b × c is a normal to the plane.

recall.must_convey: That b × c is at right angles to both given vectors and therefore is a normal to the plane.
accept: b cross c is at right angles to both so it is the normal
the plane is parallel to b and c so their cross product is the normal
take n as b cross c
b cross c ni normal ga theeskovali
a vector perpendicular to both is perpendicular to the plane

steps.why: A plane parallel to two directions has those directions lying in every parallel copy of it, so a vector at right angles to both is at right angles to the plane.
common_mistakes: Adding b and c instead of crossing them.
Using b or c on its own as the normal.

steps.label: Find b × c
steps.margin_note: Two marks. b on the top row, c below. The j term is −(−5 − 12), so it comes out positive and large.
steps.memory_tip: The j bracket is −(−5 − 12) = +17, the largest number in the answer.

lines.text: n = b \times c = \begin{vmatrix} i & j & k \\ 1 & -2 & 4 \\ 3 & 2 & -5 \end{vmatrix}

accept: expand the determinant to get two i plus seventeen j plus eight k
the normal is two seventeen eight
b on top and c below in the determinant
b cross c equals two i plus seventeen j plus eight k
the j term is plus seventeen

steps.why: The j term carries two minus signs, one from the expansion and one from the arithmetic, so it turns positive. That is the single place this determinant goes wrong.
common_mistakes: Writing the j term as −17 by keeping only one of the two minus signs.
Putting c on the top row, which reverses the whole normal.

steps.label: Find a · n
steps.margin_note: Fifth mark. Only the point goes into this dot product. The two direction vectors have dot product zero with n, which is a useful check later.
steps.memory_tip: Only the POINT goes in here. The directions would each give zero.

accept: dot the point with the normal to get minus thirty six
six minus thirty four minus eight is minus thirty six
a dot n is minus thirty six
a dot n minus thirty six vasthundi
the constant is minus thirty six

steps.why: This number is the constant term of the plane. It depends on the point, which is exactly what separates this plane from every plane parallel to it.
common_mistakes: Dotting b or c with n, which gives 0 and a plane through the origin.
Sign slip on the −2j and −k components.

steps.label: Write the vector equation
steps.margin_note: Sixth mark. One line, and the paper may ask for this form alone.
steps.memory_tip: The plane is every r with the SAME dot product against n that A has.
lines: The plane is r·n = a·n, that is

recall.must_convey: That the vector equation is r·(2i + 17j + 8k) = −36.
accept: the vector equation is r dot two i plus seventeen j plus eight k equals minus thirty six
r dot n equals a dot n
write the plane in r dot n form
r dot n equals minus thirty six ani rasta
every point of the plane has this dot product

steps.why: The vector form is the shorter answer and is complete on its own. The Cartesian form is a substitution away.
common_mistakes: Writing r·n = 0, which is a different, parallel plane.
Leaving the constant on the left as +36.

steps.label: Write the Cartesian equation
steps.margin_note: The last two marks. Two checks are available here and both are one line: the point must satisfy the equation, and each direction must give zero against the normal.
steps.memory_tip: Two checks: the point fits the equation, and each direction dots to zero.
lines: parallel to b and to c.

recall.must_convey: That the Cartesian equation is 2x + 17y + 8z + 36 = 0, that A satisfies it, and that b·n and c·n are both zero.
accept: the plane is two x plus seventeen y plus eight z plus thirty six equals zero
the point satisfies it and both directions dot to zero
substitute r as x i plus y j plus z k for the Cartesian form
b dot n and c dot n rendu zero, so parallel confirm
two x plus seventeen y plus eight z equals minus thirty six

steps.why: A direction parallel to a plane has dot product zero with its normal. Testing both directions checks the cross product, and testing the point checks the constant.
common_mistakes: Checking the point but never the two directions.
Moving the −36 across without changing its sign.
